session.title: Cutting AI Agent Costs with Azure Cosmos DB: The Agent Memory Fabric
session.abstract:
Multi-agent AI systems are exploding in 2026—but they're bleeding money.

This talk reveals how we rebuilt our entire architecture using Azure Cosmos DB as a unified "Agent Memory Fabric"—combining vector search for semantic caching, Change Feed for event-driven coordination, and optimistic concurrency for conflict prevention. The result: cost reduction, sub-100ms agent handoffs, and zero state conflicts.

session.title: Distributed Locks, Sagas, and Coordination with Cosmos DB
session.abstract:
In distributed systems, "just put a lock around it" sounds reasonable until you add retries, multiple regions, and a job that can run twice. Under real load you get duplicate processing, stuck workflows, and race conditions that only appear when everything is slow and concurrent.

In this session I'll show you how to use Cosmos DB as a coordination mechanism for distributed workflows, from basic lock/lease and leader-style patterns to saga orchestration for long-running work. We'll focus on the correctness tradeoffs teams run into in production including contention, hotspots, retries, and how consistency choices affect what your system can safely assume across regions.

name: Justine Cocchi
bio: Justine is a Principal Program Manager on the Azure Cosmos DB team at Microsoft. She focuses on improving programmability for the API for NoSQL and enhancing developer experiences to help make customers more successful. This includes experiences with the change feed, caching and materialized views.

session.title: Mastering the Azure Cosmos DB Change Feed: Patterns, Scaling, and Real-World Architectures
session.abstract:
Change Feed is one of Azure Cosmos DB's most powerful features—a persistent, ordered log of all changes to your data that enables event-driven architectures, materialized views, and real-time synchronization. This session dives into how the Azure Cosmos DB Change Feed works under the hood and how to use it effectively in production scenarios.

We'll walk through common consumption models, partitioning and lease management, and debugging and monitoring techniques for the most frequent failure modes teams encounter when running change feed processors at scale. The session includes a demo of a real-world change feed app including how to diagnose lag and recover processing. We'll close by illustrating how advanced features like global secondary indexes build directly on these same change feed patterns to turn proven architectures into fully managed capabilities.

name: James Codella
bio: James is a Product Manager in Azure Cosmos DB working on NoSQL Query, vector search, and AI products. He has more than 15 years of experience working in data, analytics, and machine learning. He has a B.S. and an M. Eng. from Cornell University and a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin - Madison in Operations Research. He currently lives near NYC with his wife and puppy.

session.title: Querying and Indexing in Azure Cosmos DB: The Complete Guide
session.abstract:
Every query in Azure Cosmos DB has two jobs: finding the right partitions and then identifying the right documents within them. Understanding how routing and indexing work together is the key to writing queries that are both fast and cost-efficient. This session provides a comprehensive guide to Azure Cosmos DB's query engine and indexing system.

We'll cover:
- Query fundamentals, including partition routing, indexing behavior, and reading query metrics
- Azure Cosmos DB SQL query language features such as joins, aggregates, subqueries, and system functions
- Index types and when to use them: range, composite, geospatial, full text, and vector indexes
- Index management, including indexing policies, index builds, and rebuild considerations
- Advanced optimization techniques such as computed properties and identifying high RU queries

Live demos throughout the session show the RU impact of indexed vs. non-indexed queries and how small indexing changes can significantly reduce cost.

What attendees will leave with:
- A clear mental model for how Azure Cosmos DB queries execute
- Practical guidance for choosing and tuning index types
- Diagnostic techniques for finding and fixing expensive queries

session.title: Performance-Boosting Memory Patterns: Save Tokens, Cut Costs, Increase Speed
session.abstract:
AI systems must retain conversation history, tool outputs, and user context across multiple turns. Basic approaches can quickly increase token usage or result in the loss of critical context.

This session will explore three memory patterns implemented using Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL:

1. Sliding Window Memory: Utilizes summarization for recent and older turns.
2. Hierarchical Memory: Combines recent context, compressed history, and long-term tiers with intelligent retrieval.
3. Entity-Based Memory Graphs: Extracts and stores structured facts for precise recall.

The session will include a practical demonstration of these patterns in action, highlighting how they enable AI applications to recall context from extended conversations efficiently, without excessive prompt size or token costs.

Key Takeaways for Attendees:
- Concrete code patterns for each architecture
- Guidance on selecting the appropriate approach
- A reusable Azure Cosmos DB schema for AI agent memory management

name: Anurag Dutt
bio: Anurag is a Cloud Engineer with expertise in multi-cloud architectures, automation, and infrastructure management across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Passionate about cloud-native technologies and open-source, he helps teams optimize cloud workloads for scalability, security, and cost efficiency. With hands-on experience in IaC, Kubernetes, and DevOps, Anurag simplifies complex cloud concepts into practical, real-world strategies for developers and engineers.

session.title: From Rising RU Costs to Stable Performance: A Practical Cosmos DB Case Study
session.abstract:
As Azure Cosmos DB workloads scale, teams often experience rising RU costs, unpredictable latency, and uneven throughput caused by early design decisions that no longer meet production requirements.

In this session, I will walk through a realistic, high-volume data ingestion and querying workload that experienced rapid cost growth and performance degradation over time. Using Azure platform metrics, diagnostics, and query insights, we will examine how issues such as hot partitions, cross-partition queries, over-indexing, and inefficient throughput provisioning were identified.

The session will then demonstrate how targeted improvements in partition strategy, query design, indexing policies, and throughput management led to measurable reductions in RU consumption and improved system stability. Each optimization will be explained through the decision-making process behind it, supported by before-and-after comparisons of cost, latency, and throughput.

Attendees will leave with a practical, repeatable framework for diagnosing and resolving common Cosmos DB performance and cost challenges.

She went on to be an early full-stack engineer at Coursera and spent many years after at Khan Academy, both as an engineer and the creator of the computer programming content.

session.title: Know your user: Identity-aware MCP servers with Cosmos DB
session.abstract:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables AI agents to securely access external data and services, but how can MCP servers store per-user data when multiple users share the same server?

In this session, we'll build a Python MCP server that authenticates users via Entra ID and stores their data in Azure Cosmos DB. I will walk through how to integrate OAuth with the FastMCP framework, use the Cosmos DB Python SDK, design partition keys for efficient per-user data isolation, and implement role-based access using Microsoft Graph group membership. I'll also share development tips when working with Cosmos DB: using the VS Code extension to explore data, chatting in GitHub Copilot with the data via the Cosmos MCP server, and empowering Copilot with agent skills to align the server code with Cosmos DB best practices.

Walk away with a production-ready pattern for building authenticated MCP servers that keep each user's data private and secure.

name: Sudhanshu Khera
bio: Sudhanshu is a Senior Product Manager at Microsoft, specializing in security for Azure Cosmos DB. Sudhanshu has over 17 years of experience in driving strategy and innovation in enterprise/B2B digital Identity and Access Management (IAM) and cybersecurity.

session.title: Securing Azure Cosmos DB: The Right Way
session.abstract:
Modern data applications often struggle to balance strong security with developer velocity. Teams face hard questions: how to move away from shared secrets, how to limit access without breaking apps, and how to protect sensitive data while still enabling real-world operational scenarios.

In this session, we'll walk through a practical, recommended approach to securing cloud data workloads. Using real customer scenarios, we'll discuss how to think about identity-first access, isolation, encryption, and data protection as a cohesive strategy rather than a collection of disconnected features.

Attendees will leave with a clear, adaptable framework for evaluating and improving their data security posture over time.

name: Divakar Kumar
bio: Divakar Kumar is a Microsoft MVP in AI and a Microsoft Certified Trainer (MCT), working as a Technical Architect at Flyerssoft. He actively shares his knowledge through blogs, talks, and training sessions, empowering developers to harness the potential of AI in real-world applications.

session.title: Real-Time Fraud Detection at Scale: Event Sourcing with Azure Cosmos DB
session.abstract: This session demonstrates three architectural patterns for building real-time decision systems with Azure Cosmos DB: Event Sourcing with hierarchical partition keys for immutable audit trails, temporal queries, and scalable event storage; Change Feed pattern for push-based event notifications that trigger instant materialized view updates without polling; and Event-Driven Integration for capturing domain events from existing databases (PostgreSQL, Oracle, MongoDB) through Azure Service Bus while keeping source systems authoritative. Through a live fraud detection demo that combines traditional ML for clear-cut cases and Agentic AI for uncertain scenarios, you'll see how these patterns enable fast decisioning, complete auditability, and seamless integration across heterogeneous data sources.

name: Yohan Lasorsa
bio: Yohan is a passionate software craftsman and open-source enthusiast who finds the web to be the ultimate playground. With expertise in full-stack engineering and a love for DIY projects, he enjoys exploring the boundaries of JavaScript and sharing his knowledge with others. As a Google Developer Expert (GDE) for Angular, Yohan is an accomplished international speaker and trainer, and an active maintainer and contributor to various open-source projects.

session.title: Beyond Vector Search: What RAG Actually Needs
session.abstract:
Your AI agent is confidently serving wrong answers, and you don't even know it. Vector search is everyone's default for RAG, but ask for something specific and it quietly returns nonsense.

In this session, we'll take a working AI agent with MCP and a real database, and extend it with agentic RAG using Azure Cosmos DB hybrid search—vector plus full-text—so it actually retrieves what matters. You'll learn why the default approach breaks, how to fix it, and how to let the agent decide when to search instead of doing it blindly every time.

Live code, live demo, patterns you can steal.

name: Jonathan Lee
bio: Jonathan Lee is a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI. He joins the Azure Cosmos DB Conf 2026 keynote as a featured guest.

session.title: Keynote Featured Guest
session.abstract: Jonathan Lee from OpenAI joins the Azure Cosmos DB Conf 2026 keynote conversation on modern applications, AI, and data at scale.

session.title: Behind the Scenes: How Azure Cosmos DB Runs Under the Hood
session.abstract: Ever wonder what actually happens between clicking "Create" in the portal and your database being ready to serve requests at planetary scale? In this session, we'll pull back the curtain on Azure Cosmos DB's internal architecture, from how we deploy our database engine onto hardware from partners like AMD in datacenters worldwide, to how we set up replica sets with quorum-based replication to deliver the high availability guarantees you depend on. We'll demystify how consistent hashing determines where your data lands and why choosing a good partition key matters so much. From there, we'll explore how we built the pay-per-request serverless model, demystifying what a Request Unit actually is under the covers. We'll also look at capabilities like RU pooling, which lets you pool throughput capacity across your workloads when running a fleet of Cosmos DB containers. We're ditching PowerPoint and going straight to the whiteboard for this one.

name: Khelan Modi
bio: Khelan Modi, a dynamic Product Manager at the forefront of the Azure Cosmos DB team, seamlessly integrates his deep expertise in databases with a passion for AI innovation. Focused on the transformative potential of vector search, Khelan consistently pioneers modern AI methodologies to enhance product functionalities across industries like advertisements and retail. His unique blend of technical proficiency and compelling presentation skills establishes him as a thought leader making impactful contributions in the realms of databases and artificial intelligence.

session.title: One Codebase, Any Cloud: Building a Retail Database with OSS and Azure
session.abstract:
Retail engineering teams face a choice that shouldn't be a choice: run your database on-premises for compliance and cost control, or move to the cloud for scale and managed operations. With DocumentDB and Azure DocumentDB, that's a false dilemma.

In this session, you'll see a complete retail store database—product catalog, inventory, orders, and vector-powered recommendations—built once using MongoDB-compatible APIs and deployed both on-prem via the DocumentDB Kubernetes operator and on Azure as a fully managed service. Same drivers. Same queries. Zero application changes.

You'll walk away with an architecture you can actually replicate, and an honest accounting of the tradeoffs at each layer.

name: Patrick Oguaju
bio:
Patrick C. Oguaju is a software engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating high-scale, cost-sensitive distributed systems on Azure.

He has worked extensively with Azure Cosmos DB in production, supporting data-intensive workloads across various industries, including retail, content platforms, and cloud-native services. His work spans data modeling, migration, performance tuning, observability, and cost optimization.

Patrick focuses on practical engineering lessons, including the trade-offs, failures, and insights that only emerge in real systems at scale, and enjoys sharing patterns that developers can immediately apply in their own architectures.

session.title: Designing Cost-Efficient, High-Scale Systems with Azure Cosmos DB: Lessons from Production
session.abstract:
Azure Cosmos DB gives developers incredible scale and flexibility, but without deliberate design, costs can spiral fast.

In this session, I'll walk through how we re-architected a real production system to dramatically reduce Azure Cosmos DB costs without sacrificing performance, availability, or developer velocity.

The session covers:
- How poor partitioning and indexing silently inflate RU consumption
- Practical data-modeling patterns that cut read/write costs
- Strategic use of TTL, Change Feed, and data tiering
- When not to use containers, indexing, or multi-region writes
- How observability exposed hidden cost leaks

The session is demo-driven and grounded in real engineering decisions from high-volume, globally distributed systems. Attendees will leave with repeatable patterns they can apply immediately to their own Cosmos DB workloads.

session.title: Data Modeling Decisions That Make or Break Your Cosmos DB Application
session.abstract:
Your data model determines your application's scalability, query performance, and cost—and the wrong choices are painful to fix later. Additionally, estimating data growth and resource requirements is crucial for preventing surprises down the line.

In this session, you'll learn:
- Strategies for choosing partition keys.
- Understand the tradeoffs in schema design.
- Estimating storage and scaling needs.
- Tips for managing cross-partition queries efficiently.

name: Sajeetharan Sinnathurai
bio: Principal Product Manager passionate about empowering developers with exceptional tools and experiences. Let's connect!

session.title: Setting Up Your Azure Cosmos DB Development Environment (and Supercharging It with AI)
session.abstract:
A well-configured development environment makes everything easier—faster iteration, reliable testing, and fewer surprises in production. This session walks through setting up a complete Azure Cosmos DB development workflow, then shows how to supercharge it with AI coding assistants.

We'll cover:
- VS Code configuration and essential extensions for working with Azure Cosmos DB
- Local development using the Azure Cosmos DB emulator, including limitations and cloud switching
- Testing patterns with the Azure Cosmos DB emulator, integration testing strategies, and CI/CD considerations
- Using context files to improve AI coding assistants' understanding of your Azure Cosmos DB schema
- Effective prompting techniques for generating better Azure Cosmos DB queries, SDK code, and data models

What attendees will leave with:
- A ready-to-use Azure Cosmos DB development environment setup
- Sample context files for AI coding assistants
- A repeatable workflow that accelerates Azure Cosmos DB development

name: Sergiy Smyrnov
bio: Sergiy Smyrnov is a Principal PM @ Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB team focusing on helping customers to solve mission critical problems with help of distributed NoSQL database technologies. Sergiy has extensive experience in database development, architecture and performance tuning across various Relational, NoSQL and NewSQL technologies.

session.title: From JOINs to JSON: Migrating a Real-World ASP.NET App to Cosmos DB with GitHub Copilot
session.abstract:
Migrations from RDBMS to Cosmos DB are notorious for hard decisions—denormalization trade-offs, partition key selection, embedded vs. referenced data, and complex application code conversion.

What if an AI agent could analyze your schema, generate a detailed migration plan, provision Cosmos DB infrastructure, rewrite your application data layer to the Cosmos SDK, and migrate your data—all through natural-language prompts?

In this session, we take the classic AdventureWorks database and an old ASP.NET EF Core Web Application and live-walk through every step of such a migration: from relational schema to a fully running .NET 9 app backed by Cosmos DB for NoSQL.

You'll leave with a reusable, prompt-by-prompt playbook and learn how to use Cosmos DB Agent Kit AI skills which you can apply to your own migrations.

session.title: Designing High-Scale Event-Driven Microservices with Azure Cosmos DB
session.abstract:
Event-driven architectures often fail at scale due to tight coupling, fragile messaging pipelines, and operational complexity.

In this session, I'll share how we designed and evolved a high-scale, event-driven microservices system using Azure Cosmos DB Change Feed as the backbone for domain events, running in production under real traffic.

We'll walk through the concrete problems we faced: synchronous service dependencies, ordering guarantees, hot partitions, and consistency trade-offs. I'll show how we modeled events per bounded context, selected partition keys that survived scale, and implemented reliable consumers using the Cosmos DB SDK.

The talk includes a live, repeatable demo that shows an end-to-end event flow: from write, to Change Feed, to downstream services, along with observability and failure handling.

Attendees will leave with practical patterns for building scalable, loosely coupled microservices using Azure Cosmos DB, plus lessons learned from real-world trade-offs and mistakes.

session.title: Memory for Your Agents: Building Chat History and Semantic Caching with Azure Cosmos DB
session.abstract:
AI agents are only as intelligent as their ability to remember. Without persistent memory, every conversation starts from scratch, costing tokens, increasing latency, and delivering disconnected user experiences. In this demo-driven session, I'll show you how to use Azure Cosmos DB as the unified memory layer for your agentic AI applications.

We'll build two essential containers from scratch: a Chat History container that preserves multi-turn conversations across sessions and devices, and a Semantic Cache container that uses vector search to return prior LLM completions for semantically similar prompts, reducing costs and latency by avoiding redundant API calls.

You'll see the data modeling decisions that matter: choosing the right partition key strategy for multi-tenant workloads, designing documents that balance write distribution with query locality, and configuring vector indexes for fast similarity search. I'll demonstrate how context windows work, why your cache needs chat history context to return accurate results, and how to implement TTL policies for automatic data lifecycle management.

Walk away with working code patterns you can apply immediately to give your agents the memory they need to deliver coherent, cost-effective, context-aware experiences.

name: Rakhi Thejraj
bio: Rakhi Thejraj is a Principal Program Manager at Microsoft, focused on Azure Cosmos DB. She specializes in data ingestion, scalability, and cost optimization for distributed NoSQL workloads. Rakhi works with enterprise customers to optimize their throughput and enable reliable, high-performance data platforms at global scale.

session.title: Importing Data into Azure Cosmos DB: Tools, Tradeoffs, and Capacity Planning
session.abstract:
You have data somewhere else and need to get it into Azure Cosmos DB—fast, reliably, and without burning through your budget. This session compares your import options and shows how to plan and execute data migrations efficiently.

We'll cover:
- Import tools and tradeoffs, including the Desktop Data Migration Tool, Azure Data Factory, and the Azure Cosmos DB Spark connector
- Capacity planning and cost optimization, including estimating RU requirements and pre-scaling for faster ingestion
- Post-import optimization techniques such as scaling throughput back down and partition merge
- Best practices for error handling, retries, validation, and indexing during bulk loads

Each tool includes a hands-on walkthrough with real data, highlighting the configuration settings that matter most for performance.

What attendees will leave with:
- A decision framework for choosing the right Azure Cosmos DB import tool
- Capacity planning calculations for bulk data loads
- Step-by-step guidance for executing efficient Azure Cosmos DB data migrations

name: Theo van Kraay
bio: Theo is passionate about NoSQL and distributed computing. He joined Microsoft in 2017 and has been in the Cosmos DB Engineering team as a Program Manager since 2019. He currently focuses on AI, programmability, and developer experience for Azure Cosmos DB. He has a masters degree in Data Science from Dundee University, and lives in the UK with his wife, two boys, and ragcoon cat.

session.title: MultiCloudDB: Write Once. Run Anywhere.
session.abstract:
Modern cloud-native databases are powerful, but each comes with its own SDK, query language, and operational model. Moving between them often means rewriting large parts of your data access layer.

In this session, we introduce a sneak preview of MultiCloudDB for Java, a portable SDK that lets you write CRUD and query logic once and run it across Azure Cosmos DB, Amazon DynamoDB, and Google Cloud Spanner, with zero code changes. By switching a single configuration setting, you can move between providers without touching application code.

We will walk through the design of the SDK, including a portable query DSL that translates into native query languages, a capability model that surfaces what is truly portable, and a provider agnostic API built for real world applications. You will also see a live demo showing the same Java application running unchanged across multiple cloud databases.

Whether you are building multi cloud systems, avoiding vendor lock in, or simplifying your data access layer, this session will show how to build once and stay portable without sacrificing the power or flexibility of cloud native databases.
